kind: declaration — stated before the read, and before the bed that the read needs exists
tier: WebGPU (X1). The CSS tier derives and is recorded beside; it gates nothing.
readAgainst: the frozen G1 endpoint, `packages/calibration/results/2026-09-10-w27c-g1-corrected-declaration.json`, resolved inactive SHA-256 351976df9bd2a2eca86aca590e6df22f4b0b1eba8cea3aba7602ccbceb9371f9 (light) and c8b338b8850da818a2931ad5f2b7da1849c942cd9bef6aefe13bc95c99ccec0b (dark). No parameter may change in response to the read.
$comment: W27 Decision Log 12 holds G2 until 'a read holds' a bound 'declared before the
read', and claims §5.130 §8 says that bound 'must confront the holdout
residuals rather than copy the calibration mean'. This is that bound.
Two things about it are deliberate. It is stated on the INTERIOR metric, not
on the full-canvas mean the hold's own 'seven to eight times' was computed on,
because that statistic mixes material error with footprint area and the
checking bed's footprint composition differs from the calibration set's by
design (decomposition.json; and claims §5.130 §1's own sentence, 'The full-
canvas mean is not an interior bound'). And its levels come from two places
outside the calibration mean: the bar the ACTIVE material is already held to,
and the frozen experiment's own VALIDATION reading — the honest measured
expectation for cells the fit never selected on.

metrics.fullCanvasDeltaE: whole-image mean per-pixel OKLab distance, the canonical `oklabDeltaE` of packages/calibration/src/metrics/perceptual.ts — the same quantity `adopted-thresholds.test.ts` gates and claims §5.130 §7 tabulates
metrics.bodyDeltaE: the same distance over the declared union eroded 6 CSS px — the mask the material occupies

clauses.name: the ceiling — per cell, full-canvas
clauses.rule: Every checking-bed cell reads `oklabDeltaEMean` at or below its profile's adopted WebGPU-tier bound.
clauses.reason: These are not new numbers and they are not derived from the inactive bed at all. They are transcribed from the TEXTURE_TIER_* tables of packages/calibration/test/adopted-thresholds.test.ts — the bar the ACTIVE material has been held to on the same tier, the same profile and the same metric since the frozen active bed was adopted. The inactive pose ships into the same product through the same root, so it may not be held to a weaker one.
clauses.whatTheRecordAlreadySays: All 30 spent holdout cells clear this, at 14%-69% of the bound; the worst is `photo__rrect-lg__inactive-tint-orange` at 0.048488 against 0.07. Clause 1 is therefore a non-regression clause, not the discriminating one — which is the honest way to say it rather than presenting a bar the endpoint already passes as if it were the test.

clauses.name: the discriminating clause — per profile, interior
clauses.rule: The checking set's equal-cell mean `bodyDeltaE` for each profile is at or below the threshold below.
reason: Each threshold is that profile's VALIDATION mean body ΔE from the frozen
G1 read, rounded up to two significant figures: 0.031024, 0.033094,
0.033466, 0.040434, 0.007716, 0.010442 (decomposition.json, computed from
results/2026-09-10-w27c-g1-corrected/checked.json).
Validation is the right level for three reasons. It is the frozen
experiment's own measured performance on cells the fit never selected on,
so it is what the endpoint's authors would have predicted for unseen cells
had they been asked. It is NOT the calibration mean — it is 1.29x to 2.18x
larger, which is the gap §5.130 §8 forbids copying away. And it is a number
the frozen bed produced, not one invented for this gate, so it cannot be
accused of having been chosen to be passable.
It is also discriminating rather than decorative, which is the property a
declared bound most needs and most often lacks. Applied to the 30 spent
holdout cells it would PASS four profiles (1x light 0.026274, 2x light
0.026908, increased contrast 0.006368, reduced transparency 0.008161) and
FAIL the two dark ones (0.066909 and 0.066844 against 0.034 and 0.041).
That is exactly the verdict the per-cell evidence supports: the light and
accessibility poses generalise, the dark one does not.

clauses.name: the per-cell floor on a named residual
clauses.rule: No checking-bed cell exceeds twice its profile's clause-2 threshold. A cell that does is named in the ledger, and no inactive floor may be adopted at G3 for the regime that cell identifies, even if its profile's mean holds.
reason: A mean over a large bed absorbs one bad cell, and every residual §5.130 §7
names is concentrated in one or two cells. 2x is the smallest multiple that
admits every VALIDATION cell of the frozen read with margin — the worst are
1.78x (1x light `photo__rrect-md__inactive-tint-orange`, 0.05689) and 1.67x
at 2x — and it would have caught both dark residuals: the mid-dark capsule
at 2.98x and the dark photo rrect-lg at 2.05x. A multiple that admits the
bed's own validation cells and catches the bed's own known failures is the
one to declare.

clauses.name: what is reported whether or not it gates
clauses.rule: The read publishes, per cell: both metrics, the resolved group state, the backdrop tone the group actually read, the geometry read-back, the native fixture's per-cell attestation including the inactive-presentation attestation, and the eroded-body level, chroma and standard deviation beside the distances. The per-profile comparison is stated on `bodyDeltaE`; the full-canvas ratio to the calibration set is reported and is explicitly NOT a gate quantity, with decomposition.json's reason cited.
clauses.reason: The statistic that produced 'seven to eight times' is a fair comparison between sets of equal footprint composition and an unfair one between sets that differ 3.4x-3.7x in it. The checking bed differs by design — it is deliberately weighted toward the large components the fit never saw — so quoting that ratio again without the footprint beside it would repeat the error this gate found.

clauses.name: what stops or refuses the read
rule: REFUSED BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN, and the scene may be recaptured inside the same session: any row whose reported canvas, requested scale and devicePixelRatio disagree; whose `problems` is non-empty; whose resolved group state differs from the declaration; whose adapter is a fallback; or whose native fixture lacks the inactive-presentation attestation. This is the corrected G1 instrument's fail-closed integrity gate, inherited.
SPENT once written and compared. A failed partial read is spent, never silently retried as fresh (W27f G1's rule, taken).

SUSPENDED if group E's re-attestation cells do not reproduce the recovered fixtures within the settle protocol's noise. That would make the recovered bed's admissibility — Decision Log 5 — the finding, and the rest of the read waits on it rather than being interpreted against a bed that has just been called into question.

STOPPED if any renderer golden, isolation hash, or either active resolved fingerprint moves. The endpoint is applied as a patch through `applyMaterialProfile`; the active material must be byte-identical throughout.

whatHoldingMeans.g2Unblocks: when clauses 1, 2 and 3 hold on every profile the checking bed covers.
whatHoldingMeans.ifOnlySomeProfilesHold: G2 stays blocked by default. Shipping the pose on the profiles that hold and withholding it on the others is a coherent alternative and it is a USER decision, not this gate's: it would mean a runtime whose activation pose is published in one colour scheme and not the other, which is a product question about what the library promises.
whatHoldingMeans.noFloorIsAdoptedHere: G1b adopts nothing. Clause 1's thresholds are the active bed's existing adopted bounds quoted for comparison; clause 2's and clause 3's are gate conditions for a read that has not happened. G3 still owns every inactive floor, and clause 3 constrains which of them it may adopt.

$comment: Recorded because a bound declared against a premise should say what it found
when it checked the premise. This is a finding, not a recommendation to
reverse anything; the ruling is the user's.
W27 Decision Log 12 holds G2 because 'today the inactive endpoint is seven to
eight times worse [on holdout] than on calibration'. That ratio is real on
the metric it was computed on and it is not a like-for-like comparison: the
holdout set's mean footprint is 3.4x-3.7x the calibration set's, because the
active split reserved exactly the largest components. On the interior mask
the ratio is 1.74x and 1.61x on the light standard profiles — BELOW those
profiles' own validation ratio of 2.05x and 1.99x — 1.01x and 1.22x on the
two accessibility profiles, and 3.47x and 3.60x on the two dark ones, where
it is carried by two cells.
So the record supports a narrower hold than the one in force: the dark
scheme's endpoint is not proven, no inactive floor is adoptable anywhere,
and the four named model-form gaps are open. It does not support 'proven on
23 cells only' as a description of the light and accessibility poses, which
clear both the active bed's adopted ceiling and their own validation level on
cells the fit never saw.
